issue: Paper claims 'latest 1K > 90%' but cross-seed analysis reports 'newest 1K = 59.1%'

resolution.the_90_percent_claim: Comes from failure curve at 5K (latest_1K = 99.0%) or matched ordering at 10K (latest_1K = 92.8%). Both are valid but describe different scales.
resolution.the_59_percent_number: Is the 3-seed MEAN of failure curve latest_1K at 10K: seeds 42 (71.9%), 2024 (51.6%), 137 (53.8%). The discrepancy is from averaging across seeds with different degradation levels.
resolution.why_matched_ordering_is_higher: eval_matched_ordering.py uses a DIFFERENT evaluation approach (mega-batch with fp16 model) than the failure curve's vendor evaluate.py. Also uses key_clustered ordering which may interact differently with cache_c. The matched ordering stream has unique-subject records only.
resolution.key_confusion: The paper likely conflates: (1) latest-1K at 5K edits (~99%), (2) latest-1K at 10K edits (59-72% depending on seed), and (3) latest-100 at 10K (80-83%). These are three different quantities.

recommendation.local_plasticity: Support 'local plasticity' with IMMEDIATE INSTALLATION efficacy, not latest-1K at the final checkpoint. Latest-1K at 10K includes edits that have already experienced up to 999 subsequent edits — not pure plasticity.

three_quantities_to_report.1_immediate_install: Efficacy of each batch right after installation (from mechanism logs)
three_quantities_to_report.2_latest_100_at_checkpoint: Latest-100 at each checkpoint (closest to 'still plastic')
three_quantities_to_report.3_latest_1K_at_checkpoint: Latest-1K at each checkpoint (broader cohort measure)

recommendation.paper_language: Do NOT say 'latest 1K remains above 90%' at 10K edits. It does not. SAY: 'At 5K edits, the newest cohort retains >99% efficacy while the oldest drops to 70%. At 10K edits, even the newest 1K cohort degrades to 59% (3-seed mean), but the age gradient remains steep — the oldest cohort falls to 7%.'
